Ondas Posts Record $167.5 Million Q3 Revenue, Raises 2026 Outlook
1 min read
ONDS
Ondas reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $167.5 million, up 100% sequentially and more than 16-fold year over year. Gross profit was $36.5 million, with a GAAP gross margin of 21.8%, while net loss was $64.7 million. The company raised its 2026 revenue target to at least $550 million and initiated a 2027 target of at least $1.1 billion.
Financial Highlights
Revenue was $167.5 million, compared with $10.1 million in Q3 2025 and $83.8 million in Q2 2026; pro forma organic revenue grew 64% year over year.
Gross profit was $36.5 million, compared with $2.6 million a year earlier. GAAP gross margin was 21.8%, and adjusted gross profit and adjusted gross margin were $58.3 million and 34.8%, respectively.
Operating loss was $189.5 million, compared with $15.5 million in Q3 2025.
Net loss was $64.7 million, compared with $7.5 million in Q3 2025. Diluted loss per share was $0.10.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $59.7 million, compared with $8.1 million in Q3 2025. Ondas expects operating-platform Adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4 2026 and company-wide profitability by Q3 2027.
Business Highlights
Formed Ondas Sentinel, combining DZYNE Technologies and World View under unified leadership to advance U.S. defense programs and the development, production, and deployment of defense technologies.
Established Regna AI to develop sovereign AI applications for defense and national security customers, using NVIDIA Nemotron models and Palantir platforms.
Expanded its land-systems portfolio and capabilities through acquisitions spanning unmanned ground vehicles, precision strike, sensing, connectivity, and navigation. The company also plans to acquire Stemme to strengthen production capacity for the ULTRA aircraft.
Advanced customer programs and product deployments, including counter-drone protection at major sports venues, a U.S. Army follow-on task order, the Digital Bat program, and the first flight of Blitz Block 3. Ondas also opened a training, testing, and flight-operations hub in Springfield, Ohio.
Original SEC Filing: Ondas Inc. [ ONDS ] - 8-K - Nov. 12, 2026

Before Trump Eased Nvidia Chip Exports to China, He Bought $160 Million in Stock, Raising Conflict-of-Interest Questions
Add preferred source
1
U.S. President Donald Trump has been revealed to have purchased $1 million to $5 million worth of Nvidia stock (approximately NT$33 million to NT$160 million) just before rescinding the Biden administration's AI chip export controls, and to have made at least three additional purchases of $250,000 to $500,000 each after opening H200 chip sales to China. An anti-corruption organization is questioning the intersection of policy shifts and personal financial interests. The controversy deepened after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid suspicions of involvement with an alleged Chinese spy. Democrats have launched an investigation, leaving Nvidia's China business prospects facing dual policy and political uncertainties.
Key Elements
Donald Trump Nvidia Jensen Huang Alice Huang DeKleptocracy U.S. Department of Commerce H200 chips AI Diffusion Framework Megaspeed The Guardian Council on Foreign Relations
U.S. President Donald Trump has been revealed to have made large purchases of Nvidia stock on the eve of rescinding the previous administration's AI chip export controls, triggering strong questions about the intersection of policy and personal financial interests. According to an analysis by anti-corruption organization DeKleptocracy of Trump's public financial disclosure filings, Trump purchased $1 million to $5 million worth of Nvidia shares (approximately NT$33 million to NT$160 million) just days before scrapping the Biden administration's "Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion" in May of last year.
The policy had originally established tiered management of AI chip exports based on each country's diplomatic and security relationship with the United States, with allies such as South Korea placed in a relatively permissive category, while China, Russia, and North Korea faced the strictest export blockades. The core purpose of the Biden administration's framework was to slow China's acquisition of advanced computing power and thereby its ability to build up its own AI capabilities. The Trump administration decided to scrap the entire framework on the grounds that it hindered American corporate innovation, imposed unnecessary regulatory burdens, and effectively relegated dozens of countries to "second-tier" status in a way that could damage diplomatic relations.
The timing overlap makes this transaction particularly sensitive. Had the framework actually taken effect, Nvidia's shipments to China—a market that once contributed about a quarter of its sales—would have been significantly constrained. After Trump announced the rescission of the controls, Nvidia's stock price promptly rose. The disclosure filings also show that Trump simultaneously purchased shares in tech giants including Apple, Meta, and Microsoft, rather than betting solely on Nvidia.
The controversy does not end there. In December 2025, Trump further announced that Nvidia would be allowed to sell H200 chips to approved customers in China, and the U.S. Department of Commerce formally granted approval in January 2026. The H200 was one of Nvidia's most advanced products at the time, with experts estimating its performance at roughly six times that of the chips China could obtain at the time. Boyuan Capital Closes RMB 1.1 Billion ($155 Million) Industrial AI Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:03 AM
Boyuan Capital Closes RMB 1.1 Billion ($155 Million) Industrial AI Fund
Boyuan Capital has completed the final close of its second fund with approximately RMB 1.1 billion ($155 million) in capital commitments.
Fund II will invest in industrial artificial intelligence, embodied intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and the international expansion of Chinese industrial companies.
The fund’s limited partners include national funds of funds, social-security funds, industrial groups, financial institutions, and local government-guided funds.
German outdoor power-equipment manufacturer STIHL also participated in the fund, expanding Boyuan Capital’s international industrial and corporate network.
The U.S. dollar amount is an approximate conversion and may vary with exchange rates.
Expanding Boyuan’s Industrial Investment Strategy
Boyuan is Bosch Group’s only market-oriented investment platform. The firm combines financial investment with access to Bosch’s engineering knowledge, value chain, industrial applications, customers, and international operations.
Fund II builds on Boyuan’s earlier investment activity across automotive technology, new energy, and intelligent manufacturing.
The new vehicle will focus more directly on applying AI within industrial environments. Boyuan is targeting technologies that can move beyond laboratory demonstrations and operate at commercial scale in manufacturing, robotics, automotive, energy, and other physical industries.
The firm plans to evaluate whether a company’s technology can solve identifiable industrial problems, be integrated into existing production environments, and generate products or services that can be delivered consistently at scale.
Boyuan will also examine whether portfolio companies can use China’s engineering and manufacturing capabilities to compete in international markets.
Creating Companies Through Industrial Partnerships
Fund II’s strategy includes creating new businesses through carve-outs and joint incubation projects connected to Bosch and other industrial partners.
A carve-out can transform a technology, operating unit, or internal project into an independent company. Joint incubation allows Boyuan to combine the technical capabilities of an established industrial group with a new management team and outside capital.
This approach is intended to give young companies access to real industrial environments earlier in their development. It may also help them validate products with potential customers before investing in broader commercialization.
Boyuan plans to identify technologies within Bosch’s value chain that could become independent businesses. The firm will also pursue joint ventures with other manufacturers and technology partners.
Seven Initial Portfolio Companies
Fund II has already invested in seven companies.
The portfolio includes Bowintec, which was jointly incubated by Boyuan and Galbot, and Weifu Smart Sensing, a company created with Weifu High-Tech and Bosch.
Boyuan has also invested in robotics companies Linkhou Robotics and Inspire Robots. These investments reflect the fund’s focus on embodied intelligence, where AI systems interact with physical environments through robots, sensors, and automated equipment.

articles.text:
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:44 AM
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
MaxCyte has agreed to acquire Akron BioProducts from affiliates of Arcline Investment Management for $151.8 million. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Akron Bio supplies Good Manufacturing Practice-grade reagents and ancillary materials used across cell therapy manufacturing. Its products include cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived materials, specialty media, and other consumables.
The acquisition will expand MaxCyte beyond its historical focus on nonviral cell engineering. Akron’s products are used in both viral and nonviral workflows at stages ranging from cell expansion through cryopreservation.
The combined company’s technologies are incorporated into five commercially approved therapies and support more than 100 clinical programs. Both businesses maintain drug master files referenced in customers’ regulatory submissions, creating long-term connections to validated manufacturing processes.
Akron is expected to produce approximately $28 million in 2026 revenue and between $7 million and $8 million of EBITDA. MaxCyte expects the acquisition to nearly double its revenue base, increase recurring consumables revenue, and accelerate its path toward profitability.
The companies have limited customer overlap despite serving similar biopharmaceutical markets. MaxCyte therefore expects to use its commercial infrastructure to introduce Akron products to additional customers and pursue cross-selling opportunities.
The buyer projects that Akron’s positive cash flow will help reduce the combined company’s annual cash burn to less than $10 million in 2027. MaxCyte expects to hold approximately $40 million to $45 million of cash when the transaction closes.
The consideration consists of $105 million in cash, subject to adjustments, 20,639,733 MaxCyte shares valued at approximately $26.8 million, and $20 million of guaranteed deferred payments. The deferred amount will be paid in two $10 million installments in January 2028 and January 2029.
MaxCyte has also secured a credit facility of up to $75 million from MidCap Financial, consisting of a $55 million term loan and a $20 million revolver. It plans to draw $20 million from the term loan and $2 million from the revolver at closing.
Akron will continue operating under its existing brand, with its management team and employees remaining part of the combined organization.
KEY QUOTES
“The acquisition of Akron marks an exciting new chapter for MaxCyte. This acquisition represents a significant step forward for us, expanding our presence across the viral and non-viral cell therapy development and manufacturing workflow, while projecting to nearly double our revenue base and accelerate our path to profitability. From day one, Akron provides us with an established portfolio of clinical and commercial programs supported by Akron’s DMFs and reagents. By bringing together two highly complementary businesses, we are diversifying our revenue base, increasing our mix of recurring revenue and expanding our exposure to the growth of commercially approved cell therapies, positioning MaxCyte for more durable near- and long-term growth. Round led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management's 1GT and Axon Partners Group, and with participation from existing and new investors.
BARCELONA, Spain , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stark Future, the Barcelona company behind the world's best-selling enduro motorcycle, today announced the close of a financing round with a total transaction value in excess of €150 million, the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. The round values Stark Future at €1.2 billion pre-money, making it Europe's first electric motorcycle company valued above €1 billion. The round was led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management's 1GT climate private equity strategy and Spain-based international investment firm Axon Partners Group, with participation from existing shareholders and friends and family. The round was oversubscribed and exceeded the initial target, prompting the Company to keep the door open for a second closing to accommodate additional strategic partners, including Lombard Odier among others.
Continue Reading
Anton Wass - CEO and Founder of Stark Future
Stark Future HQ - Barcelona
Stark VARG SM_Lineup
Anton Wass, Production line Barcelona HQ
Founded in 2020 on an uncompromising belief that electric motorcycles should not just be the green alternative, but the better machine, Stark Future builds bikes designed to beat the best combustion competitors in every category they enter. Today, the VARG platform, spanning motocross, enduro and supermoto, is designed, engineered and built in-house at the Company's 20,000 m² facility on the outskirts of Barcelona. The new capital will fund global expansion and the development of new electric platforms.
In just three years of sales, Stark has gone from challenger to category leader. The VARG is now the best-selling enduro motorcycle on the planet, outselling every combustion competitor. Within its first year, Stark took around 50% of the enduro market in Germany and the top spot in France and Italy, while the United States has grown to be its largest market by volume. From a standing start, Stark has taken around 5% of the €3 billion global off-road motorcycle market from combustion in three years. The new capital is aimed at repeating that, and more, by entering new motorcycle categories, in a much larger €90 billion addressable motorcycle market. Few hardware companies grow this fast. Fewer do it profitably.
Anton Wass, Founder and CEO of Stark Future, says: "Six years ago, Stark was an unwavering belief that electric could be the better machine, not the compromise. Today it's the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. Calibrant Energy Secures $145 Million in Project Financing, Including Battery Storage for Hyperscale Data Center Customer in PJM
News provided by
Calibrant Energy
Nov 10, 2026, 09:02 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Investec-led financing recapitalizes operating assets and funds new construction projects
BOSTON , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Calibrant Energy, a leading provider of on-site energy solutions, today announced the close of a $145 million debt facility led by Investec for solar and battery storage projects across multiple U.S. power markets. The portfolio includes a 120 megawatt-hour (MWh) battery energy storage system (BESS) serving a hyperscale data center customer in PJM. Citi , Liberty Bank, and Siemens Financial Services also participated in the facility.
Data center operators are looking for ways to get online faster as PJM and federal regulators work through how large power users connect to the grid. Calibrant's engineered BESS solutions give energy-intensive facilities greater control over how and when they draw power. This flexibility supports faster interconnection timelines and reduces the need for costly grid infrastructure upgrades that would otherwise be passed on to other ratepayers.
"Data center operators are choosing on-site energy storage because it is a fast, reliable, and effective way to get online and operate as responsible grid citizens," said Phil Martin, CEO of Calibrant Energy. "With this financial close and site mobilization for a hyperscale data center, Calibrant continues to demonstrate that large-load flexibility is not just possible but a commercial reality today."
Calibrant's turnkey, zero-capex solutions unlock the path to reliable power that the world's largest power users need to grow their businesses.
"Investec is proud to support Calibrant and Macquarie on this transaction," said Fred Petit, Co-Head of Energy & Infrastructure North America at Investec. "We value the opportunity to partner with experienced investors and operators, and to provide financing that advances the energy transition and the critical infrastructure needed to meet growing power demand across the U.S."
Calibrant Energy now has more than 5.9 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage capacity in operation, in construction, or under exclusive development agreements, including additional sites with the same hyperscale customer. This growth reflects rising demand from large power users for on-site energy solutions that accelerate speed to power while easing strain on the grid. It also reflects customers' preference for a trusted, experienced partner that can develop, own, and operate these solutions and deliver the power outcomes their business plans depend on.
About Calibrant Energy : Calibrant Energy is a leading provider of on-site energy solutions for large power users. Calibrant's turnkey, zero-capex solutions unlock the paths to power that the world's largest power users need to grow their businesses, while enabling a more reliable, affordable, and sustainable power grid. As the trusted on-site energy partner to many of the world's largest enterprises, Calibrant has more than 2.2 GW / 5.9 GWh of projects in operation, construction, or under exclusive development agreements. Calibrant is backed by Macquarie Asset Management. Learn more at www.calibrantenergy.com
